title: How does the memory keep growing without becoming unreadable?
context: Today each project has a board (decisions plus typed entries), and the Crux roll-up keeps a cross-project conventions list. Nothing yet holds what is known about you, and nothing tidies the board as it grows. Every new orchestrator reads the indexes first, so their size is what each agent pays to get started.

options.name: Project boards only
options.summary: Keep what exists. Each board grows on its own; the index-first loading from decision 11 keeps start-up cost down. Your profile is a separate file agents are told to read.

cons: A lesson learned in one project never reaches the others
Old memos pile up; nobody merges them
The profile is outside the system, so it goes stale

options.name: Three layers, tidied at each handoff
options.summary: You (profile), all projects (conventions), this project (board). Agents load the three short indexes. When an orchestrator hands off, it also proposes tidy-ups: merge old memos, retire stale ones, and promote anything that holds beyond this project up a layer. Promotions into your profile come to you as one batch card.

pros: Lessons travel: a rule learned on Ebb reaches AcuLoad
Tidying rides on handoffs, which already happen, so no extra agent or schedule
You only see changes to your own profile, batched
cons: Tidy-ups only happen as often as handoffs do

options.name: Three layers plus a librarian agent
options.summary: Same layers, but a separate low-cost agent runs on a schedule (say nightly) to turn the event log into entries, merge duplicates and propose promotions.
options.sketch: <svg viewBox='0 0 320 180'><rect x='20' y='18' width='160' height='36' rx='6' fill='var(--accent)' fill-opacity='0.85' stroke='currentColor'/><text x='100' y='40' font-size='12' text-anchor='middle' fill='currentColor'>You (profile)</text><rect x='20' y='72' width='160' height='36' rx='6' fill='var(--muted)' fill-opacity='0.35' stroke='currentColor'/><text x='100' y='94' font-size='12' text-anchor='middle' fill='currentColor'>All projects</text><rect x='20' y='126' width='160' height='36' rx='6' fill='var(--muted)' fill-opacity='0.35' stroke='currentColor'/><text x='100' y='148' font-size='12' text-anchor='middle' fill='currentColor'>This project</text><rect x='215' y='60' width='90' height='60' rx='6' fill='var(--muted)' fill-opacity='0.35' stroke='currentColor' stroke-dasharray='4 3'/><text x='260' y='87' font-size='12' text-anchor='middle' fill='currentColor'>Librarian</text><text x='260' y='101' font-size='12' text-anchor='middle' fill='currentColor'>nightly</text><line x1='213' y1='90' x2='182' y2='90' stroke='currentColor' stroke-dasharray='4 3'/><polygon points='182,90 188.3,87.0 188.3,93.0' fill='currentColor'/><line x1='213' y1='105' x2='182' y2='140' stroke='currentColor' stroke-dasharray='4 3'/><polygon points='182,140 183.9,133.3 188.5,137.3' fill='currentColor'/><line x1='213' y1='75' x2='182' y2='36' stroke='currentColor' stroke-dasharray='4 3'/><polygon points='182,36 188.3,39.0 183.5,42.8' fill='currentColor'/></svg>
pros: Board stays tidy even on projects with few handoffs
Can catch things the orchestrator never wrote down
cons: One more agent spending your plan on a schedule
Reads everything, so it can promote things you never meant to keep
More to build and to trust

criteria.name: Start-up cost per agent
criteria.note: B and C add two short indexes

recommendation: It gives the memory somewhere to grow (upward) and a regular moment to tidy itself, without a new scheduled agent. A librarian can be added later if boards outgrow handoffs.

settles.value: three layers: personal profile, cross-project conventions, project board; agents load each index first; tidy-ups and promotions proposed at every orchestrator handoff, profile changes batched for the human
